title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals
summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving supervisors a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks they must supervise.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff with a working understanding of blockchain technology and the crypto-asset ecosystem, and the analytical tools to assess business models, identify red flags and supervise the sector effectively.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a comprehensive, practical grounding in how blockchain technology works and how crypto-asset markets, products and service providers operate. Participants leave able to analyse business models and their economic function, identify the key prudential, conduct and financial crime risks, and apply risk-based judgement to digital finance scenarios.
sections.What It Covers: Blockchain technology, crypto-asset typology and market structure, wallets and custody, virtual asset service providers, tokenisation, stablecoins and unbacked crypto-assets, DeFi and emerging technologies, supervisory risks, financial crime and the travel rule, and digital finance strategy and policy.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and authorisation staff responsible for, or moving into, oversight of virtual asset service providers
Risk, policy, legal and financial crime specialists working on digital finance
Senior managers shaping the authority's approach to crypto-assets and digital finance
Learning Objectives: Explain how blockchain and distributed ledger technology operate within digital finance
Analyse crypto-asset types and business models to determine their economic function and risk profile
Evaluate the supervisory risks of custody, tokenisation and stablecoins
Assess the activities, governance and controls of virtual asset service providers
Apply AML/CFT requirements, including the travel rule, to crypto-asset activity
Evaluate emerging trends and policy choices that balance innovation with effective risk management
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about four hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines technical explanation with case studies, red flags and supervisory question exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision, authorisation or financial crime work is helpful. No technical background in blockchain or crypto-assets is required.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
Basel Committee, Prudential Treatment of Cryptoasset Exposures (2022)

modules.title: Foundations of Blockchain Technology
modules.summary: An introduction to how blockchains record and validate transactions, and the advantages, trade-offs and limitations of decentralised ledgers compared with centralised databases.
objectives: Explain how blockchain technology operates in practice
Analyse consensus mechanisms and their implications
Evaluate technological limitations and scalability challenges
syllabus: Distributed ledgers: how data is recorded and validated across networks
Blocks, hashing and immutability: how cryptography protects integrity
Proof of work, proof of stake and other consensus mechanisms
Public, private and permissioned networks: use cases and limits

modules.title: Crypto-Assets and Market Structure
modules.summary: The typology of crypto-assets and the structure of crypto markets, following the money to understand how value is created, transferred and traded across centralised and decentralised platforms.
objectives: Classify the main types of crypto-asset
Analyse market structures, incentives and trading dynamics
Evaluate risks associated with different market participants
syllabus: Cryptocurrencies, utility, governance and security tokens
Exchanges, brokers, market makers and institutional participants
Centralised exchanges versus decentralised trading platforms
Liquidity, price formation and market fragmentation risks

modules.title: Wallets, Custody and Key Management
modules.summary: How control of crypto-assets rests on cryptographic keys, the custody models firms use to safeguard client assets, and the operational and governance risks supervisors should test.
objectives: Explain how private keys determine control of assets
Evaluate custody models and their risks
Assess operational and cyber risks in custody arrangements
syllabus: Public and private keys: how asset control works
Hot, cold, hardware, multi-signature and custodial wallets
Segregation, reconciliation and safeguarding of client assets
Key loss, hacks and system failure: lessons from custody incidents

modules.title: Virtual Asset Service Providers
modules.summary: The roles, activities and business models of virtual asset service providers, and the challenges of defining and policing the regulatory perimeter around them.
objectives: Identify core service provider activities and services
Analyse business models and revenue sources in crypto markets
Assess perimeter, licensing and registration considerations
syllabus: Exchanges, brokers and trading platforms: operating structures
Custodians, wallet providers, issuers and token platforms
Infrastructure providers supporting crypto-asset markets
Hybrid and decentralised models: perimeter implications

modules.title: Tokenisation
modules.summary: How traditional financial assets are represented on distributed ledgers, the legal, operational and technological considerations involved, and the supervisory challenges as market structure evolves.
objectives: Explain the main tokenisation models
Analyse tokenised asset and fund structures
Evaluate the legal and operational risks of tokenisation
syllabus: Tokenising real-world assets: equities, bonds and funds
Smart contracts governing asset behaviour and transfer restrictions
Claimed benefits: efficiency, transparency and liquidity
Legal enforceability, settlement finality and custody risks

modules.title: Stablecoins and Unbacked Crypto-Assets
modules.summary: The design, uses and risks of stablecoins compared with unbacked crypto-assets, with a focus on reserves, redemption and the conditions under which a peg can fail.
objectives: Classify stablecoin types and distinguish them from unbacked crypto-assets
Evaluate reserve, liquidity and redemption risks
Assess governance, disclosure and oversight requirements
syllabus: Fiat-backed, crypto-collateralised and algorithmic stablecoins
Use cases in payments, trading and settlement
Reserve composition, redemption mechanics and stress scenarios
De-pegging, governance failures and transparency red flags

modules.title: DeFi and Emerging Financial Technologies
modules.summary: The technologies reshaping digital finance, including smart contracts, decentralised finance, interoperability and digital identity, and their implications for supervision and policy.
objectives: Explain smart contracts and decentralised finance
Analyse interoperability and integration challenges
Evaluate the risks and opportunities of new technologies
syllabus: Smart contracts and automated transaction execution
DeFi protocols: lending, exchange and yield structures
Bridges, interoperability and cross-chain risk
Digital identity, on-chain credentials and AI in digital finance

modules.title: Supervisory Risks in Crypto-Assets and Digital Finance
modules.summary: A structured framework for identifying and assessing risks across digital finance, showing how market, operational, cyber and governance risks interact within firms and markets.
objectives: Identify the key risk categories in digital finance
Analyse operational, cyber and governance risks in crypto firms
Evaluate market volatility and market abuse risks
syllabus: Market volatility, leverage and price dynamics
Operational failures, cyber threats and attack vectors
Governance and control failures: lessons from firm collapses
Market abuse and manipulation in crypto markets

modules.title: Financial Crime and AML/CFT Risks
modules.summary: Financial crime risks in crypto-asset markets and the application of AML/CFT frameworks, including blockchain analytics, privacy-enhancing technologies and the FATF travel rule.
objectives: Explain AML/CFT obligations for virtual asset service providers
Apply travel rule requirements and recognise implementation challenges
Evaluate transaction monitoring and blockchain analytics tools
syllabus: Illicit finance typologies in crypto-asset ecosystems
Blockchain tracing and analytics: capabilities and limits
Mixers, privacy coins and privacy-enhancing technologies
FATF Recommendation 15 and the travel rule in practice

modules.title: Digital Finance Strategy and Policy
modules.summary: Brings the programme together to examine how tokenisation, stablecoins and DeFi affect a jurisdiction's digital finance strategy, and how authorities can balance innovation with effective risk management.
objectives: Explain the trends shaping the future of digital finance
Compare regulatory approaches and international standards across jurisdictions
Evaluate policy options, supervisory capability and resourcing needs
syllabus: Comprehensive crypto-asset regimes, convergence and divergence across jurisdictions
International standards: FSB, IOSCO, FATF and the Basel Committee
Institutional adoption, stablecoins in payments and tokenised infrastructure
Workshop: balancing growth, market integrity and supervisory capability

related.title: Crypto-Asset Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An advanced twelve-module programme equipping supervisors to authorise, supervise and take action against crypto-asset firms under comprehensive regimes and international standards.

related.title: Digital Money: Stablecoins, Tokenised Deposits and CBDCs
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and central bankers to assess stablecoins, tokenised deposits and CBDCs, and their risks to payments and financial stability.

related.title: MiCA Essentials for Supervisors (EU Edition)
related.summary: A six-module essentials programme giving EU national competent authority staff a practical command of MiCA, from token regimes and CASP authorisation to supervision and enforcement.

related.title: Supervising Crypto-Asset Service Providers under MiCA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An advanced fifteen-module programme equipping EU national competent authorities to authorise and supervise crypto-asset service providers and token issuers under MiCA.

related.title: Tokenisation of Financial Markets
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess tokenised securities, funds and collateral, DLT market infrastructure, settlement finality, custody and smart contract risk.

related.title: Quantum and Cryptographic Resilience
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping supervisors to assess firms' exposure to quantum threats, cryptographic inventories and post-quantum migration plans, and to set proportionate expectations.
